messages:
ryan_support: FYI — ACME reported ~5 users that were removed from Okta still have the 'admin' role in our app after a SCIM deprovision. They say Okta shows them deleted from the group and user list.

maria_cs: ugh, customer is on our SCIM group->role mapping flow (group externalId -> role). reported around 14:12 PDT. any quick ideas? :thinking_face:

alex_se: Can you paste the SCIM event payloads or a sample? Need to confirm whether Okta sent a DELETE or a PATCH that removed group membership.

ryan_support: Attached a snippet from Okta system log (redacted):
```
Event: SCIM Push
Timestamp: 2024-10-09T21:11:02Z
Request: PATCH /Users/00u1abcd
Body: { "operations": [ { "op": "replace", "path": "groups", "value": [] } ] }
Response: 200 OK
```
They also forwarded our audit log showing we processed the PATCH but did not remove the role mapping for those users.

alex_se: Ok. Two quick hypotheses: 1) our SCIM mapper uses group.externalId and Okta is pushing group.displayName only, so map missed. 2) our deprovision code path only removes roles on explicit DELETE user events, not on group membership updates. both have happened before.

maria_cs: customer did mention they recently renamed groups in Okta and also enabled nested group push. Could nested groups be the cause?

okta-bot: Note: Okta SCIM connector v2 will send nested group membership flattened into user's groups array only if "Push Groups" is enabled with "Include members of nested groups" checked. If groups are renamed, externalId may differ depending on connector config.

alex_se: If Okta renamed a group but kept immutable id different, externalId could be stable — but some orgs map externalId to displayName during push. Can you check the SCIM mapping on their Okta integration?

ryan_support: Customer confirmed they had a custom mapping that set group.externalId = group.displayName (so it changed). They pushed a rename two days ago. Searching our DB: the affected users have role entries linked to role_assignment.source = 'scim-group' and source_id = 'okta:engineering-admins' (old displayName). After rename the mapping started writing 'okta:eng-admins-v2' and we no longer matched to remove the old assignments on membership removal.

alex_se: That explains the orphaned role rows. Two-pronged fix: 1) short term: run a cleanup that looks for scim-group role assignments whose source_id no longer corresponds to any currently-mapped Okta group externalId for that org, and remove assignments for users not present in current membership payloads. 2) long term: update docs and add tolerant matching in our mapper (also normalize displayName vs externalId and prefer immutable oktaGroupId where available).

maria_cs: Customer wants a safe repro and timeline so they can show auditors. Can we give them steps and ETA?

alex_se: Repro steps (safe, read-only first):
1) In Okta sandbox, create group "eng-admins-old" and add user alice@example.com.
2) Confirm SCIM push adds role in our app (role_assignment record with source 'okta:eng-admins-old').
3) Rename group to "eng-admins" in Okta if their mapping uses displayName-for-externalId.
4) Remove user from group or delete user. Observe that our system receives a PATCH with groups: [] but the role_assignment remains because source_id changed to 'okta:eng-admins' and we don't retro-match.

Note: If your Okta connector is configured to include immutable group ID (okta.id) in push payload (externalId), the issue won't reproduce.

ryan_support: For the customer we probably need both a rollback script and an account-level configuration change.

deploy-bot: Scheduled job queued: scim-orphaned-role-cleanup for org:acme-corp at 2024-10-10T02:30:00Z — requires approval.

alex_se: I'll do the following: 1) run a dry-run cleanup query and paste results here for approval, 2) push a small mapper change to prefer okta.groupId if present, and 3) update the SCIM troubleshooting doc. Dry-run will list candidate role_assignment ids and user emails. ETA: 4 hours.

maria_cs: Approved — please include estimated window and backup (DB snapshot) before any deletions.

ryan_support: Customer notified that we're investigating, provided repro steps and ETA 4h for dry-run. They asked: could token scope cause this? they saw a 403 once in log.

alex_se: If we got a 403 from our SCIM endpoint while processing an Okta push, we'd reject the change. But in this case we have 200 OK from our endpoint. The 403 they're referencing was from a separate API call to our role-management service (internal) — caused by scim-service-token missing groups:write scope during a specific maintenance window. That would have been logged around 2024-10-07T05:22Z and would have caused transient failures. Not related to the rename/orphaning.

maria_cs: Good to clarify for auditors. Keep me looped; I'll coordinate with customer for approval on the deletion window.

alex_se: Dry-run results (sample):
- role_assignment id: ra_87321 user: bob@example.com source_id: okta:engineering-admins (no match in current Okta groups)
- role_assignment id: ra_87322 user: alice@example.com source_id: okta:engineering-admins-old
Actions: propose to delete ra_87321, ra_87322 if corresponding user not in group membership in Okta API.

ryan_support: thumbs-up from customer to proceed with cleanup during their low-traffic window 2024-10-11 02:00-03:00 UTC. Please ensure DB snapshot and that you emit audit events for deletions.

alex_se: Will run cleanup with --dry-run then --commit, capture SQL, and create a PR for the mapper change. I will also add a verification step in the SCIM consumer: when a group.externalId changes we should create an alias entry mapping the old id -> new id for 30 days to allow graceful drift.

maria_cs: thanks team. I'll close the loop with ACME after cleanup and share the auditor summary (repro steps + actions).

okta-bot: Tip: recommend customers include group.id in mapping to avoid displayName drift.

ryan_support: closing notes: assigned to alex_se for action items + deploy-bot scheduled job. Will post final confirmation when cleanup completes. :white_check_mark:
